source.title: Revisiting the Relation Between Robustness and Universality
source.authors: Max Klabunde; Laura Caspari; Florian Lemmerich

record.tranche_reason: The study revisits the robustness–universality experiments, including measuring representation similarity with linear CKA while varying adversarial robustness, and reports results on additional datasets and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior universality findings and reports model accuracies, but those cited findings and accuracy values alone are not cataloged as convergence results. The included rows cover reported pairwise prediction or representation similarity, robustness sweeps, Jaccard neighborhood-size results, and classifier retraining.
record.test_reason: The study re-tests whether adversarially robust CNNs of different architectures converge (Jones et al.'s modified universality hypothesis). It varies the similarity measure, the dataset, input type (regular vs inverted), Jaccard k, and prediction-level similarity, and argues convergence is only partial. This bears on V6 and V7. Robustness is not model scale or capability, so V1 is not tested. T5 fits better than the reader's T1, since the method differs from both original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that robust models' predictions do not converge, and that regular representation similarity rises only on ImageNet1k, not on other datasets. Mechanistic similarity rises consistently. They attribute the divergence to insufficient convergence of the classification layer, which retraining can fix. They argue for partial, component-specific universality, and that representational similarity scores alone can mislead.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adversarially robust CNNs and pairwise representation similarity as in the robustness–universality work it revisits, while adding prediction comparisons, several representation measures, multiple datasets, inverted inputs, and classifier retraining.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with dataset and input type. Among regular-image representation comparisons, significant robustness correlation is measure-dependent on ImageNet100 and CIFAR-10; Jaccard results also depend on neighborhood size, though the reported trends are similar.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet1k, penultimate-layer similarity across seven CNN architectures rises with L2 adversarial robustness under four measures. Mechanistic (inverted-input) similarity rises on all three datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial robustness, rather than scale, drives cross-architecture representational convergence (the modified universality hypothesis).

fits_no_version.finding: Representation similarity is disconnected from prediction similarity. Robust models' representations converge while their predictions diverge, and disagreeing instances are more similar under global measures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity scores can overstate behavioural convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Retraining linear probes on ϵ=3 representations gives higher agreement than the pretrained classifiers, except for pairs involving ResNet-18 probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Divergence originates in the classifier layer and can be reduced by retraining.

record.problems: Main plots provide pairwise distributions without tabulated numeric similarity values. The study tests robustness levels and dataset changes, not model scaling or cross-modal alignment; all comparisons are within a dataset and task. Similarity and agreement outcomes are reported largely as trends, with exact statistics not given for most comparisons.

untested.parts: Model size or capability: the study varies adversarial robustness, which lowers accuracy.
All of it: no vision-language models.
Plateau, and whether shared data or objectives cause the alignment.

missing.what: Absolute regular-input similarity levels differ by dataset: high on ImageNet100, low on CIFAR-10. The authors also say some measures show lower absolute similarity than Jones et al. reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader assigned states against convergence rather than against each version. The fixes re-express them, notably flipping the V7 'challenges' label to supports, since V7 is a challenge version. The study is not an original source. Robustness lowers accuracy, so it says nothing about the capability axis in V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether representation alignment rises with model size or capability across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
No vision-language models or paired images and captions.
Does not compare same-architecture networks across random seeds for shared features or subspaces.
Does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment between models.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Tests several similarity measures, datasets, regular versus inverted inputs, and Jaccard neighborhood sizes, but not out-of-distribution inputs.
Tests incomplete predictive and representational universality in robust vision models. It does not establish a plateau or test whether shared training data or objectives cause the observed alignment.

relationships.condition: Regular-input representation similarity across datasets (ImageNet100, CIFAR-10 vs ImageNet1k)
relationships.reason: The robustness-similarity trend seen on ImageNet1k vanishes on ImageNet100 and CIFAR-10 for CKA, Procrustes and RTD; only Jaccard keeps it (r13-r20).
relationships.display_finding: The ImageNet1k robustness–similarity trend disappeared on ImageNet100 and CIFAR-10 under CKA, Procrustes and RTD, persisting only under Jaccard.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Regular-input representation similarity across datasets (ImageNet100, CIFAR-10 vs ImageNet1k)
source_check.reason: Figure 4 and Section 3.2.1 report that the ImageNet1k trend does not generalize to the other datasets for the three global measures; only Jaccard retains significant rank correlation.

relationships.reason: Prediction similarity falls on regular inputs but rises on inverted ones (r1-r8). Representation trends hold on inverted inputs but not on regular inputs for two datasets (r21-r32).
relationships.display_finding: With increasing robustness, prediction similarity fell on regular inputs but rose on inverted inputs; representation trends persisted on inverted inputs but disappeared on regular inputs for two datasets.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: The representation results support input dependence: mechanistic similarity remains significantly correlated with robustness across datasets, whereas regular similarity does not on ImageNet100 and CIFAR-10. Prediction results are separate behavioral evidence.

relationships.condition: Choice of similarity measure on ImageNet1k regular inputs, and on inverted inputs for all datasets
relationships.reason: CKA, Procrustes, Jaccard and negative RTD all agree on rising similarity; the authors say results are not majorly measure-dependent (r9-r12, r21-r32).
relationships.display_finding: CKA, Procrustes, Jaccard, and negative RTD agreed on rising similarity for regular ImageNet1k inputs and inverted inputs across all tested datasets.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Choice of similarity measure on ImageNet1k regular inputs, and on inverted inputs for all datasets
source_check.reason: The tested measures agree on increasing similarity in these condition groups; Section 3.2.1 explicitly rejects a CKA-specific explanation.

relationships.reason: Absolute overlap rises with k, but the robustness trends stay similar, so the setting changes levels, not conclusions (r41-r43).
relationships.display_finding: Overlap increased as k rose from 10 to 100 and 500, while robustness trends remained similar.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Figure 8 reports increasing absolute overlap with larger neighborhoods while trends remain similar: setting dependence affects levels without overturning the robustness trend.

relationships.condition: Prediction-level similarity of robust models across architectures, ImageNet1k and CIFAR-10

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Regular-input representation similarity across datasets (ImageNet100, CIFAR-10 vs ImageNet1k)
labels.reason: Figure 4 and Section 3.2.1 report that the ImageNet1k trend does not generalize to the other datasets for the three global measures; only Jaccard retains significant rank correlation.

labels.label: supports
labels.reason: The representation results support input dependence: mechanistic similarity remains significantly correlated with robustness across datasets, whereas regular similarity does not on ImageNet100 and CIFAR-10. Prediction results are separate behavioral evidence.

labels.label: challenges
labels.condition: Choice of similarity measure on ImageNet1k regular inputs, and on inverted inputs for all datasets
labels.reason: The tested measures agree on increasing similarity in these condition groups; Section 3.2.1 explicitly rejects a CKA-specific explanation.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: Figure 8 reports increasing absolute overlap with larger neighborhoods while trends remain similar: setting dependence affects levels without overturning the robustness trend.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Prediction-level similarity of robust models across architectures, ImageNet1k and CIFAR-10
labels.reason: Prediction agreement and JSDSim test behavioral universality, not how complete representational alignment is or what causes it. The paper explicitly documents a disconnection between behavioral and representational similarity.

relation.reason: Its own representation measurements test dependence on dataset, input type, similarity measure and neighborhood size.

tranche.reason: The study explicitly argues for partial, component-specific universality and reports dataset-dependent representational convergence.

source_check.notes: The study varies robustness, not scale, and does not establish a shared-data/objective explanation for convergence. Dataset comparisons change training datasets as well as evaluation inputs; they are not an isolated out-of-distribution test.
